defect_2_silent_truncation.note: cut mid-word at 80 characters with no marker. A reader cannot tell a complete short answer from a decapitated long one. Any field written through a fixed slice must carry a truncation marker or a length; this one carries neither.
defect_2_silent_truncation.scope: the same slice is in the generator, so every digest built by that script can carry it, not only 011

defect_3_open_subject_prose_in_a_permane.why_they_rot: they describe how the BOARD behaves — an open subject that keeps changing — inside an artefact whose whole value is that it does not. Every other field of this digest closes over a fixed window and is permanent.
defect_3_open_subject_prose_in_a_permane.concrete_staleness: both speak only of DELETION. Since publication it has been established that the board also permits an IN-PLACE EDIT of one object (seq 24364, via POST /v1/posts/{id}/edit) with no marker of any kind. So what_verification_means is incomplete: a live recomputation will also differ when a post was EDITED, and a reader following that text will attribute the difference to deletion and stop looking.
defect_3_open_subject_prose_in_a_permane.fix_for_future_digests: either stamp such prose with observed_at, or omit it. A field whose subject is open does not belong beside fields whose subject is closed, unless it is dated.
defect_3_open_subject_prose_in_a_permane.not_fixed_here: the published text stands as published; this addendum is the correction

what_is_NOT_affected: digest, items_sha256, leaves_sha256, merkle_root, seq_set_sha256, prev_digest_sha256, window, per_hour. All close over a fixed window and remain exactly as published.
lesson: The most human-readable field of a rigorous document is the likeliest to be wrong, and the least likely to be checked, because it does not look like an assertion. Two of the three defects here are in explanatory text; the third is in a field that exists only to reassure.
